clue.text: With distressed cry acted as a baby

indicators.note: something distressed is upset and jumbled, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wailing in distress behaves like an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges CRY ACTED AS; 'baby' is a noun for a timid person, as in 'don't be such a baby'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby, in the sense of a cowardly person, is the playground taunt for a timid coward.

clue.text: Inclination members have to support military command

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath and holds up the first

parts.note: an inclination is a slant or slope
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: A tilt of the limbs is needed to back up an order on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'have to support' puts ARMS below SLOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a drill order telling soldiers to rest their rifles on their shoulders.

clue.text: State extreme characters might be in shortly

definitions.text: State extreme characters might be in shortly

parts.words: State extreme characters might be in shortly
parts.note: the postal abbreviation of this US state consists of the first and last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A country's leading figures could be arriving soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' points at the state's two-letter abbreviation, AZ: the alphabet's extreme characters.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state is abbreviated AZ, the first and last letters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Person without convictions questioned

parts.note: an undecided respondent in an opinion poll, rather than someone with a clean criminal record being interrogated

explanation.surface: A suspect with no previous record is interviewed by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convictions' suggests a criminal record, but means firm opinions: the poll answer of the undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollsters label undecided respondents by the reply they give, lacking any firm opinion.

clue.text: Vacillating women long mocked? It's generally accepted

indicators.note: wavering back and forth, so these letters shift into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Indecisive women who have long been ridiculed ask whether something is widely agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacillating' rearranges WOMEN LONG MOCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everyone knows and accepts as true is information shared by the general public.

clue.text: Island republic sailor turned up in

indicators.note: the sailor's letters go inside the republic's name

parts.note: Togo is a republic in West Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so its letters reverse

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives at an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: AB stands for able seaman; in a down entry 'turned up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, part of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Realise opening of Three Sisters will captivate university

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: the opening letter of 'Sisters', taken three times

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer at Chekhov's play realises the start will enthral students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three Sisters' is read as three copies of the initial of 'Sisters', SSS; 'will captivate' puts U inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something, informally, is to work it out or realise it.

clue.text: Conical construction Yank's sweetheart put on head

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is put on top of the second

parts.note: sugar is an American term of endearment, as the clue's 'Yank's' signals
loaf is British slang for the head, as in 'use your loaf'

explanation.surface: An American's girlfriend places something on her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank's' marks the American endearment; 'put on' places SUGAR above LOAF in the down entry. 'Use your loaf' is British slang for using your head.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined sugar was once moulded into a tall cone, and the name now describes any such conical shape.

clue.text: Jam and milk

definitions.meaning: a jam is a tight ..., a crush of people
to milk is to extract money or advantage

explanation.surface: A breakfast table with preserves and dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze is a jam or crush, and to squeeze someone is to milk them for money.

clue.text: Ignoramus: all but uprooted aromatic plant

indicators.note: something uprooted is torn up and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
everything except the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An ignorant gardener has torn up almost every fragrant herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' drops the last S of IGNORAMUS, and 'uprooted' rearranges IGNORAMU.
explanation.definitionFit: Origanum is the botanical genus of marjoram and oregano, fragrant herbs.

clue.text: Extremely influential person's a huge bore

definitions.meaning: a powerful figure in an organisation
a large-calibre weapon, one with a wide barrel

explanation.surface: A powerful VIP is also tediously dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy artillery piece has a wide bore, and by extension the phrase names an important figure.

clue.text: Without working becomes beefeaters' commander

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An unemployed man becomes head of the Tower guards.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeomen Warders of the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An exon is one of the officers commanding the Yeomen of the Guard, the royal bodyguard.

clue.text: Small group with information about a way to produce beautifully designed beds

parts.note: a knot is a small cluster of people

indicators.note: the information word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A small team, given instructions on how to create lovely flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' suggests furniture but means flower beds; 'gen' is informal British for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot garden is a formal plot whose low hedges form intricate interlaced patterns.

clue.text: They hold traveller up — American gun is effective in securing article

indicators.note: holding something in place, so the gun word encloses the article

parts.note: rod is American slang for a pistol
a is the indefinite article
something that works is effective

explanation.surface: A highwayman story: an American pistol stops a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They hold traveller up' sounds like robbers but means repairs that delay motorists. 'securing' puts A inside ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to the highway delay drivers, holding up traffic.

clue.text: A way used when bogged down to avoid committee

definitions.text: A way used when bogged down

parts.note: to duck something is to avoid it
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sidestep a stuck committee meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bogged down' sounds like a stalled meeting but means literally in a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatted planks are laid over mud to make a walkway across wet ground.

clue.text: Integrally included with part of the range

parts.note: a kitchen range, a cooking stove, includes an oven

explanation.surface: Something built into part of a mountain chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests mountains but is the kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Something woven into a fabric is an integral part of it, as threads are.

clue.text: Untouchable regularly seen about to go off, shunning the light

indicators.note: the selected letters go around the other piece
taking every other letter, at regular intervals

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour

explanation.surface: An outcast is often seen about to depart, avoiding daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untouchable' looks like the subject but is the source of the alternate letters; milk that goes off is said to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal creatures are active at night and avoid daylight.

clue.text: Allowed to be named

definitions.meaning: permitted, having a right to something

explanation.surface: Being permitted to be identified.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means having a right to something, the other having a title given.

clue.text: Object flying right off in Worcester, say

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken off

parts.note: a flying saucer is a supposed alien craft

explanation.surface: A UFO is spotted over an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcester is an English city, but here it is Worcestershire sauce, the spicy condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester sauce is one example of a savoury condiment, a type of relish.

clue.text: A drunk will swap front of lounge for small bar if really necessary

indicators.note: one letter is exchanged for another
names what replaces the letter

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker

indicators.note: the front is the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of lounge
a tap is a small bar, a taproom

explanation.surface: A tipsy patron leaves the lounge for the public bar when he has to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will swap' and 'for' replace L, the 'front of lounge', in LUSH with TAP.
explanation.definitionFit: At a push is a British idiom meaning only if strictly needed.

clue.text: Shocking Franco, a little woman is leading national heroine

indicators.note: the first piece goes in front of the rest

parts.note: Jo is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women

indicators.note: something shocking is outrageous, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A scandalous dictator, with a small woman in front, a heroine of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco' looks like the dictator but is just anagram fodder; Jo March is the heroine of Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national heroine led armies against the English and was burned at the stake.

clue.text: Dutch beer's superior, swimmer found

indicators.note: in a down clue, the beer is placed above the next piece

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Dutch, as in 'my old Dutch', is Cockney slang for a wife

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a better-quality Dutch lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' puts ALE above WIFE in the down entry. 'Dutch' for wife is old Cockney slang, from 'duchess'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alewife is a North American fish of the herring family, a swimmer.

clue.text: Needing a drink to direct rehearsal

parts.note: someone thirsty is dry
to run something is to direct it

explanation.surface: Someone needs a pint before managing a practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial performance before the real thing is a practice run.

clue.text: Conductor has to stop backing poor old violin section

parts.note: to bar is to stop

indicators.note: going backwards, so the run of pieces after it reads in reverse

parts.note: ill means poor, as in ill health
the ribs are the side pieces of a violin

explanation.surface: An orchestra's leader must halt a feeble, aged violin section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses ILL + O + RIB to make BIROLLI. Sir John Barbirolli led the Hallé Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbirolli was a famous British orchestra conductor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Lover's knot, so-called

indicators.note: named that by sound, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a bow is a knot tied with loops

explanation.surface: A love knot, as it is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called' signals the sound: a bow said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer.

clue.text: Young foreign student gives a cheerful impression

parts.note: feeling up means feeling happy
an air is an appearance or impression

explanation.surface: A young overseas pupil seems happy.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreigner living with a family, often to learn the language.

clue.text: Removal of Democrat with vote about to be cut

indicators.note: a letter is removed from the vote word

parts.note: an election is a vote
C, from circa, means about

explanation.surface: A Democrat is ousted at a vote that is about to be curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut' removes C (circa, 'about') from ELECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A deletion is the act of removing something.

clue.text: Fish left by dock, caught earlier in lake

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the next

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: what is left once the second word has gone

parts.note: a haddock is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish is landed beside a dock, caught in a lake earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by dock' means HADDOCK with DOCK removed, leaving HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Chad is a large lake in central Africa.

clue.text: Lazy so-and-so we enrolled needs sorting out

indicators.note: the letters require putting into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy student we signed up has to be dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs sorting out' rearranges WE ENROLLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is an idle, worthless person.
